---
title: "Apple Browning: Analysis Code"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ri2)
library(randomizr)
library(estimatr)
library(broom)
```

## 1. Randomization before cutting

```{r}
set.seed(42)

assignment <- data.frame(
  slice_id = 1:100,
  group = sample(rep(0:3, each = 25))
)

print(assignment)
table(assignment$group)
```

## 2. Data Preparation and Outcome Distribution

```{r}
scores <- read.csv("scores.csv")

treat <- merge(assignment, scores, by = "slice_id", all.x = TRUE)

stopifnot(nrow(treat) == 100, !anyNA(treat$browning))

treat$condition <- factor(
  treat$group,
  levels = 0:3,
  labels = c("Control", "Lemon soda",
             "Bottled lemonade", "Fresh lemon juice")
)
```

### Table 1. Outcome Distribution

```{r}
outcome_table <- table(
  treat$condition,
  factor(treat$browning, levels = 0:2)
)

knitr::kable(
  outcome_table,
  col.names = c("Score 0", "Score 1", "Score 2")
)
```

### Figure 1. Outcome Distribution

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, dpi=300}
fig1 <- ggplot(treat, aes(condition, fill = factor(browning))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    stat = "count",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    vjust = -0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_grey(name = "Browning score") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Distribution of Browning Scores by Treatment Condition",
    x = "Treatment Category",
    y = "Number of apple slices"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13)
  )

ggsave("Fig1.pdf", plot = fig1, width = 10, height = 6)

fig1
```

## 3. Hypothesis Testing

```{r}
# H1: Bottled lemonade vs control
h1 <- subset(treat, group %in% c(0, 2))
h1$D <- as.integer(h1$group == 2)
fit1 <- lm(browning ~ D, data = h1)

# H2: Fresh lemon juice vs control
h2 <- subset(treat, group %in% c(0, 3))
h2$D <- as.integer(h2$group == 3)
fit2 <- lm(browning ~ D, data = h2)

# H3: Lemon soda vs control
h3 <- subset(treat, group %in% c(0, 1))
h3$D <- as.integer(h3$group == 1)
fit3 <- lm(browning ~ D, data = h3)

# H4: Bottled lemonade vs fresh lemon juice
h4 <- subset(treat, group %in% c(2, 3))
h4$D <- as.integer(h4$group == 2)
fit4 <- lm(browning ~ D, data = h4)

# H5: Lemon soda vs fresh lemon juice
h5 <- subset(treat, group %in% c(1, 3))
h5$D <- as.integer(h5$group == 1)
fit5 <- lm(browning ~ D, data = h5)

declaration <- declare_ra(N = 50, m = 25)

set.seed(42)

ri1 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                  declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = 0,
                  sims = 10000, data = h1)

ri2 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                  declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = 0,
                  sims = 10000, data = h2)

ri3 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                  declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = 0,
                  sims = 10000, data = h3)

ri4 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                  declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = 0,
                  sims = 10000, data = h4)

ri5 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                  declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = 0,
                  sims = 10000, data = h5)
```

## 4. Confidence Interval Estimation

```{r}
set.seed(42)

ate1 <- coef(fit1)["D"]
ate2 <- coef(fit2)["D"]
ate3 <- coef(fit3)["D"]
ate4 <- coef(fit4)["D"]
ate5 <- coef(fit5)["D"]

ri_ci1 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                     declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = ate1,
                     sims = 10000, data = h1)

ri_ci2 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                     declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = ate2,
                     sims = 10000, data = h2)

ri_ci3 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                     declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = ate3,
                     sims = 10000, data = h3)

ri_ci4 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                     declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = ate4,
                     sims = 10000, data = h4)

ri_ci5 <- conduct_ri(browning ~ D, assignment = "D",
                     declaration = declaration, sharp_hypothesis = ate5,
                     sims = 10000, data = h5)

ci1 <- 2*ate1 - quantile(ri_ci1$sims_df$est_sim, c(0.975, 0.025))
ci2 <- 2*ate2 - quantile(ri_ci2$sims_df$est_sim, c(0.975, 0.025))
ci3 <- 2*ate3 - quantile(ri_ci3$sims_df$est_sim, c(0.975, 0.025))
ci4 <- 2*ate4 - quantile(ri_ci4$sims_df$est_sim, c(0.975, 0.025))
ci5 <- 2*ate5 - quantile(ri_ci5$sims_df$est_sim, c(0.975, 0.025))

intervals <- rbind(H1 = ci1, H2 = ci2, H3 = ci3,
                   H4 = ci4, H5 = ci5)

colnames(intervals) <- c("CI_lower", "CI_upper")
```

## 5. Testing and Estimation Results

### Table 2. ATE Estimates, Standard Errors, Confidence Intervals, and Randomization Inference

```{r}
results <- data.frame(
  Hypothesis = paste0("H", 1:5),

  Comparison = c(
    "Lemonade vs control",
    "Fresh lemon vs control",
    "Soda vs control",
    "Lemonade vs fresh lemon",
    "Soda vs fresh lemon"
  ),

  ATE = unname(c(ate1, ate2, ate3, ate4, ate5)),

  SE = c(
    summary(fit1)$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"],
    summary(fit2)$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"],
    summary(fit3)$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"],
    summary(fit4)$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"],
    summary(fit5)$coefficients["D", "Std. Error"]
  ),

  CI_lower = intervals[, "CI_lower"],
  CI_upper = intervals[, "CI_upper"],

  RI_p = c(
    summary(ri1, p = "two-tailed")$two_tailed_p_value,
    summary(ri2, p = "two-tailed")$two_tailed_p_value,
    summary(ri3, p = "two-tailed")$two_tailed_p_value,
    summary(ri4, p = "two-tailed")$two_tailed_p_value,
    summary(ri5, p = "two-tailed")$two_tailed_p_value
  )
)

knitr::kable(results, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 6. Results Visualization

### Figure 2. Individual Outcomes and Estimated Group Means

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, dpi=300}
summary_df <-
  treat |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  do(tidy(lm_robust(browning ~ 1, data = .))) |>
  mutate(browning = estimate)

browning_plot <-
  ggplot(summary_df, aes(condition, browning)) +
  geom_point(
    data = treat,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.1),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)),
    nudge_x = 0.18,
    size = 4
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.2, 2.2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Mean Apple Browning by Treatment Condition",
    x = "Treatment category",
    y = "Apple Browning Score (0–2)",
    caption = paste(
      "Small circles = Individual apple slices",
      "Black dots = Group means",
      "Vertical lines = 95% confidence intervals for group means",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0)
  )

browning_plot

ggsave("Fig2.pdf", plot = browning_plot, width = 10, height = 6)
```
